summary: Literature lookup completed: Folding π (arXiv:2403.09277, §3) identifies Fujimoto folds as L(t)=t/2 and R(t)=(t+1)/2, cycling numerators by inverse doubling modulo an odd denominator, not as Egyptian-fraction summands. PROVED: three such folds give (t+j)/8, so a three-fold fixed point has denominator dividing 7; from a dyadic starting crease all finite outputs remain dyadic. Consequently '4/p in three folds' is neither exact for general p nor equivalent to three unit fractions; no Egyptian-fraction connection was found in the targeted search.
not_done: No claim about unrestricted origami axioms; the obstruction concerns only Fujimoto edge-to-crease bisections.

summary: EVIDENCE: trained a small boosted-tree partial-factor ranker only on 4,380 exhaustively labelled instances (p≤5000, C≤8), and evaluated 28,928 larger instances with 100001≤p≤10^6. Among 7,465 mixed feasible/infeasible instances, first-choice success is 99.06% versus 38.74% for smallest partial divisor and 45.02% random, with AUC 0.9857; comparisons use identical p and C, hence exact mod-840 matching. Success remains 97.80% on 3,086 cases with two unassigned prime slots (only 28 have three slots); this is a small learned-ranking experiment, not a neural/BP run or an existence proof. See part7 memo §Z1227 and summary.json.
not_done: No neural architecture, wall-time speedup claim, large-C generalisation, or comparison against exact modular dynamic programming; suffix labels use exhaustive enumeration.
next: Compare ranking cost against exact modular subset-product DP at larger C and more remaining factors.

summary: CERTIFIED (computer): implemented all seven Salez equations with reconstructed positive A,B,C,D and the stated gcd checks, then censused all 5,761,455 primes ≤10^8 with each constant parameter ≤24 in 171.3 CPU seconds. Exactly 16 odd primes remain uncovered by this bounded menu; 14a alone covers 5,761,255, while reversing the first-firing order assigns 5,628,567 primes to 15d. Increasing the parameter bound to 48 covers every odd prime ≤10^7, illustrating both truncation and ordering effects. Full first-firing counts by p mod 840 are in census_1e8_K24.csv; this is a declared reconstructed ordering, not recovery of Salez’s original code.
not_done: Original verification source/order not located; no 10^9 census (linear extrapolation ≈28.5 CPU minutes for K24 alone, beyond remaining per-item cap); no exhaustive unbounded-parameter census.
next: Compare families at equal search cost rather than treating first-firing labels as intrinsic prime structure.

summary: Fetched and searched the full CANT 2024, 2025, 2026 abstract PDFs (635, 1132, 1177 extracted lines) and INTEGERS 2025 abstracts (1385 lines). Three relevant talks occur: Kovač–Tao on Ahmes-series irrationality (CANT 2025), Collier Gaiser on unit-fraction Rado numbers with f2(k)=O(k^3) (CANT 2026), and Rishika Agrawal on reciprocals of shifted Golomb primes (INTEGERS 2025); CANT 2024 has no keyword match. Exact URLs and abstract excerpts are recorded in memo §Z1434.
not_done: No 2027 or ELAZ scan; the requested first-step years were fully searched, but talks were not watched and claims were not independently proved.

summary: CERTIFIED (computer): transcribed all 56 families in Cao–Xu Tables 2.1/3.1/3.2 into JSON and independently synthesized/verified 48 positive integer-valued three-denominator identities plus 8 composite factorisations using SymPy. All polynomial images cover every m residue mod 840, 1680 and 3360, but this is existential modular compatibility, not an integer covering. A separate genuine fixed-parameter progression test certifies 23/35 n≡1 (24) classes mod 840, 46/70 mod1680, 92/140 mod3360 and 1104/1680 mod40320, eventually past recorded intercept thresholds. The machine-readable formulas, denominators, integrality tests and exact scopes are in families.json and memo §Z1518; no proof of the paper’s global union claim results.
not_done: Tables 4.1/4.2 use a different 36-family Howerton numbering and are not part of the 56-family census; no full positive-integer union proof or replay to m=10^11.
next: Use the explicit JSON certificates to compare genuine progression coverage with existing identity menus, keeping modular images separate.

summary: Built Walnut from firetto/Walnut using Java 17 (the default Java 21 was incompatible with Gradle 7.5), then encoded powers of four by the regular language 0*10*. CERTIFIED (computer): Walnut returns TRUE for coverage of 4^s+9 by the proved menu n≡0 (5) or n≡13 (20), and FALSE for that same menu on 4^s+297. The direct positive-integer ES encoding was actually submitted and rejected with “the operator * cannot be applied to two variables”; finite congruence-menu coverage is automatic, but unrestricted witness multiplication is not available in Walnut arithmetic. Commands, automata, error trace and the menu identities are preserved.
not_done: No proof/refutation of ES for 4^s+297, no claim that every richer encoding is impossible, and no 15·2^s+1 attempt.
next: Walnut can verify any supplied finite regular menu; an unbounded Diophantine search requires additional arithmetic input, not merely a base-4 encoding.

summary: Assembled complete sibling counts from repo witness tables: S(n,−4) has 6/99999 failures through 10^5, Gaussian ES_Q1 has 6/39175 through norm 10^6, and 8/n has 6/2999 through 3000. Assessment: an explicit 181×181 hierarchical Beta–binomial posterior gives median population failure rate 0.000753 (95% interval 0.000141–0.0351), with finite 1000-trial predictive failure probability 0.3669. Its stationary infinite-tail P(any ES counterexample beyond 10^18)=1 is forced by the model’s positive-rate support, not by arithmetic evidence; adding an independent zero-rate ES spike leaves the answer at its arbitrary prior (0.9/0.5/0.1 in the sensitivity run). Thus the fit is completed, but finite heterogeneous sibling tables do not identify a defensible real-world posterior for ES.
not_done: No justified transfer/extrapolation law from sibling domains to ES beyond 10^18; no ES verification history likelihood or arithmetic dependence model.
next: Specify and independently validate a nonstationary zero-law and ES-specific prior before interpreting an infinite-tail posterior.
